title: Cloud Computing & Kubernetes
summary: Rent computers by the second instead of owning them, then let software keep your apps alive without a human babysitting them.

blocks.markdown:
Cloud means renting someone else's data center on demand, billed by usage — and Kubernetes keeps your containers alive on top of it.

- You stop buying servers and start buying **capacity by the second**.
- The shift is **capex → opex**: pay per second of use, scale up and down freely.
- **Containers** package an app and its deps; **Kubernetes** runs them across many machines.
- The win is **elasticity** plus **self-healing** — no human babysitting required.

blocks.subTitle: Service models
blocks.markdown:
Three service models trade **control for convenience** — each step up hands more to the provider.

| Model | You manage | Example |
|---|---|---|
| IaaS | OS upward | EC2 VM |
| PaaS | Just your code | Heroku |
| SaaS | Only your data | Gmail |

More layers handed off means less work but less flexibility.

blocks.subTitle: The four primitives
blocks.markdown:
Every cloud is built from four building blocks.

- **Compute** — runs code: VMs, containers, serverless. Measured in vCPUs and RAM.
- **Storage** — keeps data: **block** (raw disk), **object** (key→blob over HTTP, S3), **file** (shared mount).
- **Networking** — connects things: VPCs, subnets, load balancers, firewalls, DNS.
- **Identity (IAM)** — who can do what; the rule is **least privilege**. The top cause of both breaches and outages.

blocks.subTitle: Regions & availability zones
blocks.markdown:
A **region** is a geographic area; inside it are isolated data centers called **availability zones (AZs)**.

- Each AZ has independent power and cooling, linked by single-digit-ms connections.
- A single AZ can fail, so **run across ≥2–3 AZs** — cheap, standard insurance.
- A whole region failing is rare; only the most critical systems replicate **multi-region**.
- Latency drives placement: put compute near users and near its data.

blocks.subTitle: Containers vs VMs
blocks.markdown:
Containers share the host kernel; VMs each carry a full guest OS.

![VM stack versus container stack](assets/c10-cloud-kubernetes/vm-vs-container.svg)

- A container image is **MBs and starts in milliseconds**; a VM is **GBs and boots in seconds**.
- Containers use Linux **namespaces** (isolation) and **cgroups** (limits) while sharing one kernel.
- VMs run a full machine on a hypervisor — stronger isolation, lower density.
- In practice you run containers **inside** VMs to get both.

blocks.subTitle: Kubernetes architecture
blocks.markdown:
Kubernetes splits into a **control plane** (the brain) and **worker nodes** (the muscle).

![Kubernetes control plane and worker nodes](assets/c10-cloud-kubernetes/k8s-architecture.svg)

- **API server** — the single front door; the only thing that reads/writes etcd.
- **etcd** — consistent key-value store holding the entire cluster state (Raft).
- **Scheduler** — picks a node for each unscheduled pod.
- **kubelet** — per-node agent that runs assigned pods and reports health.

blocks.subTitle: The key objects
blocks.markdown:
Four objects do most of the work, in an ownership chain.

![How Deployment, ReplicaSet, Pods, and Service relate](assets/c10-cloud-kubernetes/deployment-relationships.svg)

- **Pod** — smallest unit; 1+ containers sharing an IP. **Disposable**: new IP on recreate.
- **Deployment** — manages stateless replicas via a ReplicaSet; does rolling updates and rollbacks.
- **Service** — stable virtual IP/DNS that load-balances across pods selected by label.
- **Ingress** — HTTP routing from outside: host/path rules and TLS termination.

blocks.subTitle: Desired-state reconciliation
blocks.markdown:
The heart of K8s: you declare the end state, controllers loop forever to make it true.

```text
loop forever:
    desired = read spec from API server
    actual  = observe current cluster
    if actual != desired:
        take one step to close the gap
```

- You never script the steps — you state the goal.
- This makes the system **self-healing**: kill a pod, the controller sees `actual=4, desired=5` and makes one.
- Recovery falls out of reconciliation; you wrote no failure-handling code.

blocks.subTitle: Autoscaling
blocks.markdown:
Two autoscalers cooperate — one scales the app, one scales the machines.

- **HPA** (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) — adds/removes pod replicas to hit a metric, e.g. 60% CPU. Formula: `desired = ceil(current * metric / target)`.
- **Cluster Autoscaler** — adds nodes when pods can't be scheduled; removes underused ones.
- **VPA** adjusts a pod's CPU/memory requests instead of replica count.
- Together: HPA wants more pods → no room → Cluster Autoscaler buys a node.

blocks.subTitle: What you trade on
blocks.markdown:
The main axes you weigh when choosing cloud and orchestration.

- **Control vs convenience** — lower in the stack (IaaS, self-run K8s) = more control, more toil.
- **Cost model** — on-demand (flexible, priciest), reserved (cheap baseline), spot (50–90% off but reclaimable).
- **Resilience vs cost** — multi-AZ is cheap and standard; multi-region adds real latency and cost.
- **Density vs isolation** — containers pack tight; untrusted workloads may need VM-level boundaries.

blocks.subTitle: When to reach for what
blocks.markdown:
Match the tool to the shape of the workload.

| Situation | Reach for |
|---|---|
| Many services, independent deploys | Kubernetes |
| One simple app, tiny team | Managed PaaS |
| Bursty event handlers | Serverless |
| A production database | Managed (RDS) |

Running K8s yourself is a real job — prefer a managed cluster when the team is small.

blocks.subTitle: Real systems & signals
blocks.markdown:
These ideas run the systems you use — and leave fingerprints when they break.

- **Google Borg → K8s** — a decade of declarative cluster management, open-sourced as Kubernetes.
- **Netflix on AWS** — multi-AZ plus Chaos Monkey killing instances to force resilience.
- **Amazon S3** — object storage at 11 nines durability by replicating across AZs ([b11-storage-systems](b11-storage-systems.md)).
- Watch **CrashLoopBackOff**, **Pending pods** (no capacity), and **OOMKilled** (limit too low) — the earliest "something's broken" signals.

The misconceptions that bite in interviews and production.

- **"K8s is just Docker at scale."** Docker runs one container on one host; K8s orchestrates many across many hosts.
- **"A pod equals a container."** A pod wraps 1+ co-located containers; the pod is the unit K8s schedules.
- **"Containers isolate like VMs."** They share the host kernel — weaker isolation; untrusted code needs a sandbox.
- **"I'll store data on the pod's disk."** Pod storage is ephemeral; use persistent volumes or external stores.
- **"Cloud is automatically cheaper."** Idle resources and **egress fees** can cost more — savings come from using elasticity.
